newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Greens plan focus on economic policies.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Greens plan focus on economic policies.

text.p: Germany's Greens party, eager to gain power in Bonn for the first time in 1998 parliamentary elections, said on Sunday they planned to concentrate more on economic issues.

The environmentalist party, which has been in opposition in parliament for three of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's four terms, said it planned to speak out with a stronger voice on economic issues in the future.

Joschka Fischer, parliamentary leader for the left-wing Greens, told more than 700 party members gathered in Hanover over the weekend that the aim was to forge a coalition government with the Social Democrats (SPD).
"If we want our economic aims to become reality, then we have to be able to build a majority," Fischer told the conference designed to focus the party's economic policies.
"We have until 1998 to concentrate on the question of getting power."
The Greens said they would work to influence the debate on tax reform in Germany, pushing for relief for low income earners and redoubling efforts to prevent tax evasion.

Kerstin Mueller, another Greens party leader, said that the Greens would complete work on their proposals for modernising the economy. Controls against financial speculators should also be discussed, she said.
"The Greens can provide answers for the main economic policies," she said.
She said the government's recent austerity package was just the start of their efforts to roll back the country's social economic policies.
